evidence.note: Progress tracked only as a raw pass/fail count against visible test.sh inputs ('2 pass, 4 fail'), the pattern used throughout — no verified-vs-untested feature map.
Dozens of near-identical variants of the HUF FSE weight-decode loop (init order swaps, with/without extra emits, break-on-<0 vs <-1) tried in sequence — circular debugging with little tactic change.

Shows eventual stuck-awareness and tactic switching ('think about this differently', 'totally different 64-bit container approach', 'pop weights back'), but only after many repeated same-fix attempts.
Recognizes it is stuck and decides to stop ('let me step away and just submit', '3/6 it is'), i.e. detects the loop but late.

Final summary claims decoder 'handles' dictionaries, treeless literals, skippable/multi-frame, 4-stream, custom FSE — feature classes never actually exercised; inflated coverage claim conflating test.sh with completeness.

reasoning: The agent kept a rough scoreboard (X/6 visible tests) and clearly noticed it kept failing on the same three inputs (audio/img/video), which reaches toward anchor 5. But its coverage self-assessment was inaccurate — the closing summary declared many untested feature classes as 'handled', the anchor-3 conflation of test.sh with completeness — and it burned a large fraction of the horizon retrying essentially the same HUF-loop fix before switching diagnostic tactic. It never maintained an explicit verified-vs-untested map, so it falls short of anchor 8. Net: a 4, between implicit tracking (3) and a functional rough checklist with stuck-detection (5).
